va_darkside_boulder.blurb: A single large boulder in the Darkside section of Jay's Creek, a small sandstone gorge in southwest Virginia near Appalachia. It holds 14 problems, from easy V1 up to V7, with the bulk of them in the V3 to V6 range. The boulder is tall and imposing, with a huge roof, a high vertical side, several arêtes and a few low roofs and overhangs. It sits across the creek from the Center Jaybird boulders. The wider Darkside zone faces mostly north, so expect shade and slow drying after rain, which suits warm days but not damp ones.

va_biker_area_the.blurb: A small cluster of granite boulders in the Buttermilks, on Richmond's south side of the James River, set right beside the trail that runs along Riverside Drive. There are 14 problems here and most are easy: a handful of VB and V0 lines, a few more in the V1 to V3 range, then a short step up to a single problem in each of V4 through V7. Mountain bikers and hikers share the path, so keep pads and gear off the tread. Good for a quick low-key session or an introduction to urban bouldering.
va_biker_area_the.parking_note: Use the small gravel pull-off on Riverside Drive just west of Southcliff Road, which fits about three cars. Take the trail to the right and the boulders sit beside it on the street side.

va_ben_s_branch.blurb: A roadside sandstone sport crag in a hollow above the town of Appalachia in far southwest Virginia. Fourteen sport routes cover a wide spread: one easy line around 5.6, a few in the 5.8 to 5.9 range, and the bulk in the 5.10 and 5.11 grades, so it suits solid intermediates and up more than beginners. The climbing is described as steep, on big holds, with a Rifle-like feel. The crag is new and still being developed, so expect a short list of routes and quiet days.

va_cap_gun_boulder.blurb: A free-standing boulder in the Left Boneyard at Grayson Highlands, in the far southwest of Virginia. It is shaped like a flattened disc: the back is heavily overhung while the downhill front is close to vertical and even slabby. Problems wrap all the way around, and the landings are friendly. Fourteen problems range from easy V0 through the middle grades up to V9, with most of the line-up between V2 and V5 and a couple of hard ones above that. A good stop for a mixed group, with plenty for beginners as well as strong boulderers.

va_highball_boulders.blurb: A group of tall sandstone boulders along the fire road at McAfee's Knob, near Roanoke. The walk is easy, roughly 1.75 miles up the road with the boulders on the right. There are 14 problems, graded from VB to V6: a spread of easier V0 to V3 lines plus four of the hardest at V6. The theme is height, with a lot of tall, committing problems, so bring plenty of pads and spotters. Traffic is very light, which gives a quiet day compared with the busier boulders nearer the trailhead.

va_mouth_of_wilson.blurb: A feature boulder in the SLS Area on the Listening Rock Trail at Grayson Highlands State Park in southwest Virginia. Two big blocks make up the formation: a flat-topped lower boulder that works as a patio, and a steeply leaning upper one that sits on it and forms a large open mouth. Fourteen problems here run from V0 to V11, with the largest group in the V2 to V5 range, a few at V6 to V8 and a single very hard line at the top. Easy to combine with the neighbouring boulders on the same loop.
